problem: LLMs struggle to perform software engineering tasks effectively, with existing approaches split between complex multi-turn agent frameworks and simpler single-turn workflow methods.
approach: Train an LLM using structured Agentless methods to learn reusable skill priors (code localization, editing, reflection), then apply these foundations to empower SWE-agents through supervised fine-tuning.
contribution: Kimi-Dev achieves 60.4% on SWE-bench Verified for workflow approaches and 48.6% pass@1 with agent adaptation, matching Claude 3.5 Sonnet performance.

problem: Causal discovery from observational data alone is ill-posed and fundamentally underdetermined.
approach: Leverage data from multiple environments with differing noise statistics and nonlinear mechanisms to uniquely identify causal graph structure by exploiting the connection between ICA and causal discovery.
contribution: First result guaranteeing complete causal graph recovery with only a constant number of environments (as few as two) and arbitrary nonlinear mechanisms.

problem: Positive-unlabeled learning research lacks standardized evaluation, with inconsistent data generation, disparate experimental settings, and divergent metrics leading to irreproducible findings.
approach: Create a unified benchmark with consistent data generation pipeline, integrated framework of 18 state-of-the-art methods, and standardized protocols across configurable sampling schemes and label ratios.
contribution: PU-Bench provides rigorous evaluation across 8 datasets (2880 total evaluations) revealing complex performance trade-offs and method robustness against label frequency variations.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models rely on pre-trained VLMs but lack systematic understanding of how VLM capabilities translate to downstream robot control performance.
approach: Introduce VLM4VLA, a minimal adaptation pipeline converting general-purpose VLMs to VLA policies using only new learnable parameters, and systematically study which VLM capabilities matter.
contribution: Reveals that VLM general capabilities are poor predictors of VLA task performance, vision encoders are critical bottlenecks, and embodied task fine-tuning doesn't guarantee control improvements.

problem: Multimodal LLMs struggle with emotion understanding due to spurious associations between emotions and irrelevant cues and hallucination of audiovisual information.
approach: Introduce EmoReAlM benchmark to quantify issues, then apply AVEm-DPO preference optimization with constructed preferences over responses with spurious associations and a regularization term penalizing text priors.
contribution: AVEm-DPO improves baseline performance by 6-19% relative in zero-shot emotion reasoning on DFEW, RAVDESS, and EMER datasets.

problem: LLM-powered agents for visual content generation operate under unrealistic assumptions of invariably successful tools, lacking performance-aware planning and adaptation.
approach: Propose PerfGuard framework with three mechanisms: Performance-Aware Selection Modeling using fine-grained tool evaluations, Adaptive Preference Update comparing theoretical and actual rankings, and Capability-Aligned Planning Optimization.
contribution: PerfGuard improves tool selection accuracy, execution reliability, and alignment with user intent for complex AIGC tasks compared to state-of-the-art methods.

problem: Generative diffusion models suffer an inevitable gap between generated and real data distributions, limiting generation quality.
approach: Propose Weak-to-Strong Diffusion (W2SD) that employs reflective operations alternating between denoising and inversion using weak-to-strong model gaps to steer latent variables toward real data regions.
contribution: W2SD significantly improves human preference, aesthetic quality, and prompt adherence across modalities; Juggernaut-XL achieves 90% HPSv2 winning rate improvement.

problem: Current multivariate time series forecasting methods either overfit channel ordering (channel-dependent) or neglect inter-channel dependencies (channel-independent).
approach: Introduce CPiRi framework with channel permutation-invariant (CPI) learning that infers cross-channel structure from data using spatio-temporal decoupling and permutation-invariant regularization training.
contribution: CPiRi achieves state-of-the-art results, remains stable under channel shuffling, and generalizes to unseen channels even when trained on only half.

problem: Multinomial logistic regression for neural decoding is limited to discrete output classes and cannot model continuous-valued outputs like time, orientation, or position.
approach: Generalize MLR to continuous output spaces via Continuous Multinomial Logistic Regression (CMLR), using Gaussian process priors to regularize smooth tuning functions for conditional density estimation.
contribution: CMLR consistently outperforms DNNs, XGBoost, and FlexCode on large-scale neural datasets from mouse/monkey visual and motor cortex, capturing multimodal and asymmetric distributions.

problem: Federated learning performance degrades under real-world data heterogeneity with distribution shifts across clients and distribution drift over time.
approach: Introduce Feroma framework using client distribution profiles to guide model aggregation and test-time model assignment via adaptive similarity-based weighting without knowing cluster identity.
contribution: Feroma achieves up to 12 percentage points accuracy gain over state-of-the-art methods across 6 benchmarks under dynamic data heterogeneity while maintaining FedAvg-comparable overhead.

problem: Vision-language models like CLIP struggle with query-based image retrieval under unseen query styles due to distribution shifts from training data.
approach: Propose Hystar using hypernetworks to generate style-adaptive singular-value perturbations for query-specific model weight adaptation, combined with StyleNCE contrastive loss emphasizing hard cross-style negatives.
contribution: Hystar achieves state-of-the-art performance on multi-style retrieval and cross-style classification benchmarks with parameter efficiency.

problem: Vision-language models generating tokens autoregressively are parameter-heavy and require full decoding, limiting efficiency and flexibility.
approach: Introduce VL-JEPA using Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture to predict continuous embeddings instead of tokens, enabling selective decoding and open-vocabulary tasks without architecture modification.
contribution: VL-JEPA achieves stronger performance than CLIP and SigLIP2 with 50% fewer parameters; supports selective decoding for 2.85x fewer operations; matches VLMs on VQA with only 1.6B parameters.

problem: Debiasing vision-language models via projection can amplify biases in unconsidered concepts, introducing unobserved bias increase.
approach: Propose rotation-based debiasing that rotates embeddings within a relevant subspace rather than removing subspaces, minimizing changes to unconsidered concepts.
contribution: Rotation-based approach mitigates unintended bias amplification while debiasing known concepts in VLM embeddings.

problem: MLLM-based embodied systems lack sufficient spatial information and fail to account for physical robot constraints, limiting practical applicability.
approach: Introduce OmniEVA with Task-Adaptive 3D Grounding that dynamically injects 3D features via gated routing and Embodiment-Aware Reasoning incorporating physical constraints into planning.
contribution: OmniEVA achieves state-of-the-art on 7 of 8 embodied reasoning benchmarks and excels in object navigation and mobile manipulation.

problem: Visual autoregressive models lack effective concept erasure techniques designed for their next-scale token prediction paradigm, creating safety gaps.
approach: Propose VARE framework using auxiliary visual tokens to reduce fine-tuning intensity, then S-VARE with filtered cross-entropy loss for precise unsafe token identification and preservation loss for semantic fidelity.
contribution: S-VARE achieves surgical concept erasure in VAR models while preserving generation quality and addressing language drift.

problem: Brain tumor segmentation with missing modalities is challenging; parallel fusion risks losing crucial shared information across modalities.
approach: Propose SMSN using Sequential Multi-modal Segmentation with Information-Bottleneck Fusion Module that sequentially extracts modality-common features while reconstructing modality-specific ones.
contribution: SMSN consistently outperforms parallel fusion baselines on BRATS18/20 with robustness in missing-modality settings and superior cross-domain generalization to brain metastasis datasets.

problem: Simulating coupled multiphysics systems is challenging due to data scarcity in coupled scenarios and low efficiency/fidelity in strongly coupled spatio-temporal systems.
approach: Propose GenCP formulating coupled-physics as probability modeling, integrating probability density evolution in generative modeling with iterative coupling and using operator-splitting theory.
contribution: GenCP enables training on decoupled data while inferring coupled physics and provides error controllability guarantees.

problem: Sequential disentanglement lacks established evaluation protocols and existing methods struggle with real-world data and complex optimization.
approach: Introduce DiffSDA using diffusion models for sequential disentanglement with latent diffusion, efficient samplers, and a challenging evaluation protocol across time series, video, and audio.
contribution: DiffSDA outperforms recent state-of-the-art methods on sequential disentanglement across diverse real-world modalities.

problem: High-fidelity, view-consistent rendering directly from point clouds without per-scene optimization remains a core challenge.
approach: Propose DiffPBR using diffusion models guided by viewpoint-projected noise constrained by scene geometry and visibility, with adaptive CoNo-Splatting for fast rasterization and residual learning.
contribution: DiffPBR improves rendered image quality by 3-5dB, reduces training time from 41 to 8 GPU hours, and increases rendering speed to 10fps.

problem: LoRA's fixed-rank design lacks flexibility for adapting different layers; dynamic methods often use heuristic metrics without matrix-wise distinction or capacity expansion mechanisms.
approach: Propose FlexLoRA with entropy-guided spectral energy evaluation for rank allocation, supporting both pruning and expansion under global budgets with zero-impact initialization.
contribution: FlexLoRA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines for parameter-efficient fine-tuning.

problem: Molecular generation at the atom level is inefficient and difficult to scale for large molecular spaces.
approach: Introduce FragFM leveraging fragment-level discrete flow matching with coarse-to-fine autoencoders for atom-level reconstruction and stochastic fragment bag strategy for handling extensive fragment spaces.
contribution: FragFM achieves better property control than atom-based approaches and introduces NPGen benchmark for evaluating natural product-like molecule generation.

problem: Language model-based preference models exhibit systematic miscalibration, overrelying on superficial features like length and style rather than substantive qualities.
approach: Investigate training data biases causing miscalibration using controlled counterfactual pairs, then propose counterfactual data augmentation (CDA) to mitigate issues.
contribution: CDA reduces average miscalibration from 39.4% to 32.5% across preference models.

problem: Standard reinforcement learning for code generation lacks explicit mechanisms for teaching critique and reflection capabilities.
approach: Propose Critique-Coder combining standard RL with Critique Reinforcement Learning (CRL) by substituting 20% of RL data with critique-focused data.
contribution: Critique-Coder-8B reaches over 60% on LiveCodeBench, outperforming DeepCoder-14B, and shows enhanced general reasoning on logic tasks.

problem: VLA models struggle to integrate multimodal reasoning with precise action generation while avoiding catastrophic forgetting of pre-trained vision-language capabilities.
approach: Introduce InstructVLA with Vision-Language-Action Instruction Tuning (VLA-IT) using mixture-of-experts adaptation to jointly optimize embodied reasoning and action generation.
contribution: InstructVLA achieves 33.3% improvement over SpatialVLA on in-domain tasks, outperforms fine-tuned OpenVLA by 96% on SimplerEnv-Instruct benchmark.

problem: Reasoning models exhibiting cognitive skills benefit from RL but cannot acquire skills not present in base models.
approach: Propose SkillFactory using self-distillation to prime skill acquisition during supervised fine-tuning by rearranging model samples into desired skill formats before RL.
contribution: SkillFactory SFT initialization helps models generalize to harder task variants post-RL and improves robustness to out-of-domain regression.

problem: Masked diffusion models generate only fixed-length sequences, limiting applicability to tasks requiring variable-length outputs.
approach: Introduce FlexMDMs extending masked diffusion to flexible-length generation by inserting and unmasking mask tokens, grounded in stochastic interpolant framework.
contribution: FlexMDMs match MDM perplexity while modeling length statistics with higher fidelity; achieve 60% higher success on maze planning; retrofitted LLaDA-8B improves math from 58% to 67% and code infilling from 52% to 65%.

problem: Characterizing the full class of neural sequence models supporting both parallelizable training and fast sequential inference remains unexplored.
approach: Define Prefix-Scannable Models (PSMs) as models whose state updates use parallel prefix scan with custom aggregation operators, unifying state space models and transformers.
contribution: PSMs retain transformer expressivity while matching state space model inference efficiency; show better length generalization on synthetic tasks.

problem: Pre-trained vision-language models face distributional shifts and catastrophic forgetting when adapting to new tasks in continual learning scenarios.
approach: Introduce NuSA-CL using low-rank adaptation constrained to approximate null space of current parameters to minimize interference with prior knowledge.
contribution: NuSA-CL preserves zero-shot capabilities while achieving competitive continual learning performance with minimal memory and computational overhead.
theme: Transfer Learning, Meta Learning, and Lifelong Learning

problem: Binary classification with instance-dependent label noise lacks efficient methods for estimating and correcting noise effects.
approach: Leverage loss correction with instance-aware scheme to bridge empirical noisy risk and true clean risk, using classification-calibrated losses.
contribution: Instance-only dependent noise model enables efficient transition rate estimation with demonstrated generalization across image, audio, and tabular data.

problem: Robots struggle to perform complex manipulation tasks without physical demonstrations or robot-specific training data.
approach: Introduce RIGVid using video diffusion models to generate demonstration videos filtered by VLMs, then extract and retarget object trajectories to robot in embodiment-agnostic fashion.
contribution: Filtered generated videos are as effective as real demonstrations for robot manipulation tasks including pouring, wiping, and mixing.

problem: Limited understanding of LLM representational spaces hinders interpretation of learning and connection to human learning processes.
approach: Frame LLMs as lossy compression optimizing information retention for next-sequence prediction objectives, characterizing compression optimality via Information Bottleneck theory.
contribution: Compression optimality predicts downstream performance on MMLU-Pro across different model families, linking representational structure to actionable insights.

problem: Muon optimizer outperforms Adam in LLM training but the underlying mechanism remains unclear.
approach: Analyze Muon through associative memory lens revealing superior performance on Value/Output weights and FFNs; explain superiority on heavy-tailed data via more isotropic singular spectrum.
contribution: Theoretical analysis proves Muon achieves balanced learning across classes independent of embeddings, whereas Adam induces large learning disparities on imbalanced data.

problem: Deep reinforcement learning sample efficiency is limited; improvements often require increased model/algorithmic complexity without principled motivation.
approach: Analyze critic network optimization landscape via eigenspectrum and condition number, revealing batch/weight normalization with distributional cross-entropy reduces condition numbers.
contribution: XQC achieves state-of-the-art sample efficiency across 55 proprioception and 15 vision-based continuous control tasks with fewer parameters.

problem: Stochastic Interpolants require direct access to target distribution samples and are unexplored in jointly optimized latent variable models.
approach: Develop Latent Stochastic Interpolants (LSI) with principled Evidence Lower Bound objective for end-to-end joint learning in latent space with optimized encoder, decoder, and latent SI.
contribution: LSI learns effective latent representations while sidesteppping simple priors of diffusion models and computational demands of high-dimensional SI.

problem: Reasoning in reranking tasks is assumed universally beneficial but its effectiveness for ranking remains systematically understudied.
approach: Systematically study chain-of-thought reasoning in rerankers across pointwise/listwise settings under supervised and RL training using diverse benchmarks.
contribution: Reasoning-augmented rerankers consistently underperform direct counterparts with 3 core limitations: miscalibration, higher variance, and instability.

problem: Time-series imputation requires reconciling global trends with local details along data trajectories efficiently.
approach: Propose TG-MSFM using ODE velocity field learning via flow matching with time-gated multi-scale velocity heads and data-consistency projection for inference.
contribution: TG-MSFM achieves competitive MSE/MAE on standard benchmarks with favorable speed-quality trade-offs.

problem: Pruning reasoning models causes performance loss due to decode-dominated nature; standard input-only reconstruction methods ignore chain-of-thought traces.
approach: Introduce Reasoning-Aware Compression (RAC) jointly reconstructing activations from input and on-policy CoT traces during pruning to integrate into existing workflows.
contribution: RAC significantly boosts pruning performance for reasoning models with integrated drop-in fix.

problem: Portrait animation with cross-identity attribute transfer typically requires paired training data rarely available at scale.
approach: Propose Durian with self-reconstruction formulation leveraging portrait video pairs within-video, using Dual ReferenceNet with spatial attention and complementary masking.
contribution: Durian enables portrait animation with attribute transfer, supports multi-attribute composition and smooth interpolation within single generation.

problem: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods like LoRA rely on matrix factorization and struggle in extremely low-parameter regimes.
approach: Propose TRAC leveraging Tensor-Train decomposition with across-layer compression, allowing cores to freeze or share across layers with lightweight controllers for flexibility.
contribution: TRAC achieves performance comparable to LoRA variants while substantially reducing trainable parameters and storage requirements across diverse architectures.

problem: Direct Preference Optimization shows inconsistent effectiveness between on-policy and static preference data across different models, motivating deeper understanding.
approach: Propose alignment stage assumption dividing alignment into preference injection (benefiting from diversity) and preference fine-tuning (favoring quality) stages with algorithm to identify boundaries.
contribution: On-policy effectiveness varies 3x between models; characterization of alignment stages generalizes across 5 models and 2 alignment methods.
